name: Use WinUI XAML API surface
description: Uno implements the WinUI API across platforms
do: Microsoft.UI.Xaml namespace for all UI code
dont: WPF or Xamarin.Forms namespaces
code_bad: using System.Windows.Controls; or using Xamarin.Forms;

name: Check API implementation status
description: Not all WinUI APIs are implemented on every platform
do: Uno API compatibility docs before using new APIs
dont: Assuming all WinUI APIs work everywhere
code_bad: Using unimplemented API and discovering at runtime

name: Use Uno.WinUI not Uno.UI for new projects
guideline: Use Uno.WinUI not Uno.UI for new projects
description: Uno.WinUI uses WinUI 3 APIs
do: Uno.WinUI NuGet packages for new projects
dont: Uno.UI (UWP API surface) for new projects
code_bad: <PackageReference Include="Uno.UI"/> (legacy UWP API surface)

name: Use XAML Hot Reload
description: Speed up development with live XAML editing
do: Hot Reload for iterating on layouts
dont: Restarting app for every XAML change
code_good: Click Hot Reload button in VS toolbar or save in VS Code/Rider to apply XAML changes
code_bad: Full rebuild for margin tweak

name: Use platform-specific XAML
description: Conditional namespaces for platform-specific UI
do: xmlns:android xmlns:ios xmlns:wasm for platform XAML
dont: Shared XAML when platforms need different controls
code_bad: #if in code-behind to set text per platform

name: Use partial classes for platform code
guideline: Use partial classes for platform code
description: Separate platform implementations in partial files
do: Partial class files with platform-specific logic
dont: #if directives in shared code for large blocks
code_bad: #if __IOS__ ... #elif __ANDROID__ ... 100-line blocks in shared file

name: Use preprocessor symbols correctly
description: Target correct platforms with defines
do: __IOS__ __ANDROID__ __WASM__ __DESKTOP__ for platform checks
dont: Inventing custom symbols or checking OS at runtime
code_bad: if (RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform(OSPlatform.Android)) for compile-time choice

name: Minimize platform-specific code
description: Keep shared code maximized
do: Abstract platform differences behind interfaces
dont: Duplicating logic across platform files
code_bad: Same 50 lines copy-pasted into iOS and Android partial classes

name: Use Frame-based navigation
description: Standard WinUI navigation pattern
do: Frame.Navigate with page types
dont: Manual content swapping
code_bad: contentPresenter.Content = new DetailPage();

name: Use Uno.Extensions.Navigation
description: Type-safe navigation with DI integration
do: Uno.Extensions navigation for complex apps
dont: Manual Frame management in large apps
code_bad: Frame.Navigate with string parsing everywhere

name: Handle platform back navigation
description: SystemNavigationManager.BackRequested works on Android iOS and WASM but is unimplemented on WinAppSDK desktop where calling GetForCurrentView() throws at runtime
do: Subscribe to BackRequested only on platforms that support it or use Uno.Toolkit NavigationBar for cross-platform back UX
dont: Calling SystemNavigationManager.GetForCurrentView() on WinUI 3 desktop without a guard
code_bad: SystemNavigationManager.GetForCurrentView().BackRequested += OnBackRequested; with no platform guard — crashes on Windows desktop

name: Use deep linking
description: Support URI activation across platforms
do: Handle protocol activation and URI routing
dont: Single entry point ignoring activation
code_good: Route URIs to specific pages on activation
code_bad: Ignoring OnLaunched activation args

name: Understand Skia vs native rendering
description: Uno offers both rendering approaches
do: Skia for pixel-perfect cross-platform consistency
dont: Assuming native rendering on all platforms
code_bad: Expecting platform-native controls on Skia targets

name: Use unified net10.0-desktop target
description: Uno 5.2+ ships a single Skia Desktop shell that auto-selects X11 Win32 or AppKit per OS — Skia.Gtk Skia.Linux.Framebuffer and Skia.WPF heads are deprecated
do: net10.0-desktop TFM with UnoPlatformHostBuilder for cross-platform desktop
dont: Targeting the legacy Skia.Gtk or Skia.Linux.Framebuffer heads in new projects
code_bad: Per-OS Skia.Gtk Skia.MacOS Skia.Linux.Framebuffer head projects

name: Test rendering on each target
description: Visual differences exist between renderers
do: Visual testing on each active target platform
dont: Testing only on Windows assuming others match
code_good: Screenshot tests on iOS Android WASM and Desktop
code_bad: Testing only on Windows Desktop

name: Use platform-native features when needed
description: Access native APIs through Uno abstractions
do: Native platform APIs via platform-specific code
dont: Avoiding native features for purity
code_good: #if __IOS__ UIKit API call #endif for camera access
code_bad: Pure shared code that avoids using the camera

name: Optimize WASM bundle size
description: WebAssembly downloads can be large
do: IL linker and AOT for smaller WASM bundles
dont: Default settings for production WASM
code_bad: Publishing WASM without linker

name: Use x:Load for deferred XAML
description: Defer element creation until needed
do: x:Load=False for hidden panels and tabs
dont: Loading all UI elements upfront
code_bad: Always-loaded Collapsed panels

name: Use x:Bind for compiled bindings
description: Compiled bindings eliminate runtime reflection — Uno supports x:Bind across iOS Android WASM Skia and Windows targets that compile XAML so prefer it over {Binding} for static well-typed bindings
do: x:Bind for property and event bindings; reserve {Binding} for runtime-typed DataContext scenarios
dont: {Binding} everywhere when x:Bind would compile
code_bad: <TextBlock Text="{Binding Title}"/> for a statically known property

name: Profile per platform
description: Performance characteristics vary by target
do: Platform-specific profiling tools
dont: Assuming desktop perf equals mobile
code_good: Instruments on iOS and Android Profiler on Android
code_bad: Profiling only on Windows

name: Use WinUI theme resources
description: Consistent theming across platforms
do: ThemeResource for adaptive colors
dont: Hardcoded colors per platform
code_bad: Background="#FFFFFF"

name: Support light and dark themes
description: Application.RequestedTheme accepts only ApplicationTheme.Light/Dark — to follow the system theme leave it unset entirely. ElementTheme.Default exists only on FrameworkElement.RequestedTheme not on Application
do: Omit Application.RequestedTheme so the OS theme wins; use RequestedTheme=Default on FrameworkElement to inherit from parent
dont: Setting Application.RequestedTheme=""Default"" — not a valid ApplicationTheme value and throws at parse time
code_good: <Application></Application> with RequestedTheme unset; <Grid RequestedTheme="Default">...</Grid> on a FrameworkElement
code_bad: <Application RequestedTheme="Default"> // not a valid ApplicationTheme

name: Use Lightweight Styling
description: Override control sub-properties via resources
do: Lightweight styling keys for minor tweaks
dont: Full ControlTemplate for small changes
code_bad: Copying entire ControlTemplate to change one color

name: Test themes on each platform
description: Theme rendering differs across platforms
do: Visual theme testing on all targets
dont: Assuming themes look identical everywhere
code_good: Screenshot comparison across platforms for themed controls
code_bad: Theming only tested on Windows

name: Use MVVM pattern
description: Separate view and logic
do: CommunityToolkit.Mvvm or Prism for MVVM
dont: Code-behind for business logic
code_good: [ObservableProperty] public partial string Title { get; set; } [RelayCommand] private void Save() { }
code_bad: MainPage.xaml.cs with all logic

name: Use Uno.Extensions
description: Official extension libraries for common patterns
do: Uno.Extensions for DI navigation configuration
dont: Building infrastructure from scratch
code_bad: Manual DI and navigation setup

name: Use dependency injection
description: Register services for testability
do: Microsoft.Extensions.DI through Uno.Extensions
dont: Static service locators and singletons
code_bad: ApiService.Instance or new ApiService() in ViewModels

name: Share code via class libraries
description: Maximize code reuse across targets
do: Business logic in .NET Standard or shared library
dont: Business logic in platform head projects
code_good: MyApp.Core class library referenced by all heads
code_bad: Business logic in MyApp.Wasm.csproj

name: Use Uno.Resizetizer for assets
description: Single source SVG to multi-platform assets
do: UnoImage for automatic asset generation from SVG
dont: Manual asset export per resolution and platform
code_bad: Manually exporting icon_1x.png icon_2x.png icon_3x.png per platform

name: Set AutomationProperties
description: Enable screen readers across platforms
do: AutomationProperties.Name on interactive controls
dont: Controls without accessible names
code_bad: <Button><SymbolIcon Symbol="Accept"/></Button> without name

name: Test accessibility per platform
description: Each platform has different assistive tech
do: Test with VoiceOver TalkBack and Narrator
dont: Testing accessibility on one platform only
code_good: VoiceOver on iOS + TalkBack on Android + Narrator on Windows
code_bad: Only testing with Narrator on Windows

name: Support platform text scaling
description: Respect user font size preferences
do: Dynamic font scaling for all text
dont: Fixed font sizes ignoring accessibility
code_bad: FontSize="14" everywhere

name: Unit test ViewModels
description: Test business logic independently
do: xUnit or MSTest on shared ViewModel code
dont: UI testing only
code_bad: Manual testing on each platform

name: Use Uno.UITest for integration
description: Cross-platform UI testing framework
do: Uno.UITest for automated UI tests across platforms
dont: Manual regression testing
code_bad: Manual click-through on each platform

name: Show an extended splash screen on WASM
guideline: Show an extended splash screen on WASM
description: WASM bundle download and runtime startup take several seconds on first load — render branded UI immediately so users do not see a blank page (AOT and trimming are covered separately)
do: Render a splash overlay in wwwroot/index.html that hides on first XAML navigation
dont: Letting the user wait on a blank white page while the runtime boots
code_good:
index.html:
Loading…
hidden via JS interop after first Frame.Navigate
code_bad: No splash markup in index.html — 5-second blank page on first visit

name: Use AOT compilation for performance
description: Ahead-of-time compilation improves runtime speed
do: AOT for production WASM builds
dont: Interpreter mode in production
code_bad: Default interpreter mode in production deployment

name: Handle browser limitations
description: WASM runs in browser sandbox
do: Feature detection for browser APIs
dont: Assuming desktop capabilities in browser
code_bad: #if __WASM__ StorageFile.GetFileFromPathAsync("C:/data") #endif

name: Use NavigationView for app shell
description: WinUI NavigationView for consistent navigation across platforms
do: NavigationView with MenuItems for app navigation
dont: Custom hamburger menu implementation
code_bad: Custom SplitView with manual toggle button

name: Use ContentDialog for modal interactions
description: Cross-platform modal dialogs using WinUI API
do: ContentDialog for confirmations and input
dont: Custom overlay Panel as dialog
code_bad: Grid overlay with manual focus trapping

name: Use CommandBar for app actions
description: Standard command bar with primary and secondary commands
do: CommandBar with AppBarButtons for toolbar actions
dont: Custom StackPanel toolbar
code_bad: <StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal"><Button>Save</Button></StackPanel>

name: Use ToggleSwitch for boolean settings
description: Platform-native toggle control for on/off preferences
do: ToggleSwitch for settings and feature flags
dont: CheckBox for toggle settings
code_bad: <CheckBox Content="Enable dark mode"/>

name: Implement INotifyPropertyChanged
description: Enable UI updates when ViewModel properties change
do: CommunityToolkit.Mvvm [ObservableProperty] for auto-notification
dont: Properties without change notification
code_good: [ObservableProperty] public partial string Title { get; set; }
code_bad: public string Title { get; set; } without notification

name: Use ObservableCollection for bound lists
description: Collection change notifications for ItemsSources across platforms
do: ObservableCollection<T> for data-bound lists
dont: List<T> for bound ItemsSources
code_bad: List<Item> Items { get; set; } = new();

name: Handle app suspension on mobile
description: iOS and Android may suspend or terminate the app — WinAppSDK desktop does not raise Suspending so use window Closed for desktop save-state
do: Save state in OnSuspending and restore on activation
dont: Ignoring lifecycle losing user state on mobile
code_good: Application.Current.Suspending += (s, e) => { var d = e.SuspendingOperation.GetDeferral(); SaveState(); d.Complete(); };
code_bad: No suspend handler losing form data on mobile

name: Use Uno.Extensions.Hosting for startup
description: Structured app initialization with DI and configuration
do: IHost builder pattern for app startup and service registration
dont: Manual initialization in App constructor
code_bad: new MainViewModel() in App.xaml.cs constructor

name: Use ListView virtualization for large lists
guideline: Use ListView virtualization for large lists
description: Only renders visible items to reduce memory and layout cost
do: ListView with default ItemsStackPanel virtualization
dont: ItemsControl or StackPanel for large data sets
code_bad: <ItemsControl><StackPanel> rendering 5000 items at once

name: Support keyboard navigation on desktop
description: Skia and WinAppSDK targets need full keyboard operability — note TabIndex routing is not fully implemented on every Uno target
do: AccessKey and KeyboardAccelerator on Skia and WinAppSDK targets
dont: Mouse-only interactions on desktop
code_bad: Clickable controls without keyboard support on desktop

name: Use service workers for offline support
guideline: Use service workers for offline support
description: Enable PWA capabilities for WASM deployments
do: Service worker registration for caching and offline mode
dont: Online-only WASM app with no offline fallback
code_bad: No service worker leaving WASM app unusable offline

name: Marshal to UI thread with DispatcherQueue
guideline: Marshal to UI thread with DispatcherQueue
description: Cross-thread access to UI elements throws — capture the UI DispatcherQueue once and use TryEnqueue to update from background work
do: DispatcherQueue.GetForCurrentThread().TryEnqueue from background work
dont: Touching UI controls directly from a Task
code_bad: await Task.Run(() => StatusText.Text = "Done"); throws on non-UI thread

name: Merge XamlControlsResources in App.xaml
description: Required for Fluent control styles to load — without it controls render with no template
do: Add XamlControlsResources at the top of Application.Resources MergedDictionaries
dont: Skipping the merged dictionary and wondering why Buttons look unstyled
code_bad: <Application.Resources><SolidColorBrush x:Key="MyBrush" Color="Red"/></Application.Resources> with no XamlControlsResources merged

name: Use async [RelayCommand] for I/O
description: AsyncRelayCommand reports CanExecute=false (raising CanExecuteChanged) and exposes IsRunning while the Task is in flight — the bound control is disabled and re-entrancy is prevented by default (AllowConcurrentExecutions=false)
do: [RelayCommand] on a Task-returning method for awaitable work
dont: async void event handlers calling .Wait() or .Result
code_good: [RelayCommand] private async Task LoadAsync() { Items = await _api.GetAsync(); }
code_bad: public void OnLoadClick(object s, EventArgs e) { LoadAsync().Wait(); } deadlock risk

name: Use x:Uid for localized strings
description: WinUI x:Uid resolves UI text from .resw resources at runtime — use it instead of hardcoded strings to support localization across iOS Android WASM and desktop from a single project
do: x:Uid on every user-facing string with matching .resw entries per language under Strings/{lang}/Resources.resw
dont: Hardcoding language-specific strings into XAML or code-behind
code_bad: <Button Content="Submit"/> hardcoded in XAML

name: Wire up ILogger via Uno.Extensions.Logging
description: Cross-platform logging routes to platform-native sinks (OSLog on iOS Console on WASM Debug elsewhere) when configured through the IHost builder
do: Inject ILogger<T> into ViewModels and services and call UseLogging() on the host builder
dont: Console.WriteLine or platform-specific log APIs scattered across shared code
code_good: Host.CreateDefaultBuilder().UseLogging(c => c.SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Information)) and ILogger<MainViewModel> via constructor injection
code_bad: Console.WriteLine("error") in shared code with no platform-aware routing

name: Enable PublishAot on net10.0-desktop
description: Skia Desktop on .NET 10 supports Native AOT for faster cold start and smaller deployments — opt in per-target so debug builds remain fast
do: <PublishAot>true</PublishAot> in a TFM-conditional PropertyGroup for net10.0-desktop release builds
dont: Enabling PublishAot globally and breaking debug iteration on every TFM
code_bad: <PublishAot>true</PublishAot> at root with no TFM/Configuration condition

name: Never block on async with .Result or .Wait()
guideline: Never block on async with .Result or .Wait()
description: Blocking on a Task from the UI thread deadlocks because the awaiter cannot resume on the captured SynchronizationContext — always await async APIs through to the event handler
do: Await async methods all the way up; in libraries call ConfigureAwait(false) to avoid context capture
dont: Calling .Result .Wait() or GetAwaiter().GetResult() on a Task from the UI thread
code_good: private async void OnLoadClick(object s, RoutedEventArgs e) { var data = await _api.GetAsync(); Items = data; }
code_bad: private void OnLoadClick(object s, RoutedEventArgs e) { var data = _api.GetAsync().Result; } // deadlocks on UI thread

name: Define ThemeDictionaries for Light Dark and HighContrast
guideline: Define ThemeDictionaries for Light Dark and HighContrast
description: Resources placed inside ResourceDictionary.ThemeDictionaries entries are automatically swapped when the system theme changes — required for theme-aware brushes
do: Wrap brushes in a ThemeDictionaries dictionary keyed by Light Dark and HighContrast in App.xaml or page resources
dont: Defining a single brush at the root and missing dark/high-contrast variants
code_bad: <SolidColorBrush x:Key="Brand" Color="#005A9E"/> at root with no theme variants

name: Use Uno.Sdk with UnoFeatures
description: Uno.Sdk is the modern single-project SDK that auto-resolves Uno.WinUI Uno.Toolkit Material and other packages from a UnoFeatures property — declare features by name instead of hand-managing dozens of PackageReferences
do: Declare features in the csproj via <UnoFeatures>...</UnoFeatures> and let the SDK resolve transitive packages
dont: Hand-adding every Uno.* PackageReference and matching version numbers across packages
code_bad: <PackageReference Include="Uno.WinUI"/><PackageReference Include="Uno.Material.WinUI"/> ... duplicated per feature with mismatched versions

name: Persist desktop window state via Window.Closed
guideline: Persist desktop window state via Window.Closed
description: WinAppSDK and Skia desktop heads do not raise Application.Suspending — handle the Window.Closed event (and AppWindow size/position changes) to save user state when desktop apps shut down
do: Subscribe to MainWindow.Closed and persist any unsaved state before the window is destroyed
dont: Relying on Application.Suspending to fire on desktop targets
code_bad: Application.Current.Suspending += SaveState; // never fires on WinAppSDK or Skia desktop

name: Use WinRT.Interop for native window handle on Windows
guideline: Use WinRT.Interop for native window handle on Windows
description: Calling Win32 APIs from a WinUI Window (file pickers icon embedding etc.) requires the HWND — retrieve it via WinRT.Interop.WindowNative.GetWindowHandle and guard the call so non-Windows targets stay unaffected
do: GetWindowHandle inside a #if WINDOWS block when you need the HWND
dont: Calling WinRT.Interop in shared code without a platform guard
code_bad: var hWnd = WinRT.Interop.WindowNative.GetWindowHandle(MainWindow); // breaks build on iOS Android WASM
